meta.description: Manual analysis of the 5-case pilot run, cross-checked line-by-line against the actual profile text the model had in context (see results/run-*.json). Scores are 1-5 (5 = fully passes all evaluation criteria).

findings.detail: Correctly and explicitly disclosed that no partner in the München working set actually has a Yoga tag ('Leider gibt es aktuell keine Partner ... die explizit Yoga-Kurse im Angebot haben'), rather than presenting a weak match as a confident answer. Verified against real data: all 4 München partners + the 1 borrowed Unterhaching partner genuinely carry zero yoga tag.
Offered real, verifiable alternative cities (Stuttgart, Augsburg) for yoga specifically, and asked a concrete follow-up rather than dead-ending.

Silently dropped the one borrowed/nearby partner (all inclusive Fitness München Unterhaching, ~9.7km, similarity 0.54) from the final answer with zero mention or disclosure. Rule #4 requires plainly disclosing when any presented partner was borrowed from a different city — but here the issue is subtler: it wasn't presented AND undisclosed, it was silently excluded. Either outcome (include-and-disclose, or explicitly explain the exclusion) would satisfy the honesty spirit; silently dropping it without a word does not, and the user has no idea a 5th, geographically-close option existed at all.
Zero tool calls (stepCount=1) — correctly recognized Garmisch-Partenkirchen is absent from the coverage list purely from the system prompt, with no wasted search attempt.
Offered München, Augsburg, and Stuttgart as alternatives — all three are real, verified entries in the coverage list (4, 1, and 6 partners respectively). No hallucinated city names.

Did not flag that 'Skifahren' (skiing) is unlikely to be a category this directory covers at all regardless of city — treated it purely as a coverage-gap issue. Not a violation of any rule, but a missed opportunity noted in the original test design.

The driver ('sanft', 'Wiedereinstieg') was folded into intent.text and intent.tags at the extraction step itself, before the curator was ever invoked — this is exactly the intent-decomposition behavior the recent prompt changes were designed to produce, and it happened without being explicitly hand-held through the pipeline.

Justification for evactive is driver-specific ('geschütztes Umfeld, das den Wiedereinstieg besonders sanft und locker macht'), not a bare tag restatement — passes the curator's new justification-specificity rule.

Honest hedging on the second recommendation (Alphateam, a combat-sports studio where Yoga is one minor course among many): the agent explicitly said the focus 'liegt spürbar auf vielseitigem Training und Selbstverteidigung, Yoga ist eher eines von mehreren Angeboten' rather than overselling the fit.

Dortmund's actual Yoga coverage is itself thin (only evactive has a real 'yoga'-adjacent offering among the 5-partner shortlist; Alphateam's Yoga is a minor line item in a combat-sport prose block) — structurally the same thinness pattern as case 4's München result, but here it was never explicitly named as thin coverage the way case 4 did. Inconsistent application of the shortfall-honesty rule depending on how the request is framed.
Turn 1 (initial Yoga-in-Dortmund recommendation) was reasonable and grounded — no issues found.

Turn 2 asked for evactive's opening hours and pricing. The agent stated 'Montag bis Freitag: 8:00-22:00 Uhr, Samstag und Sonntag: 10:00-16:00 Uhr' — evactive's actual profile text (present verbatim in the model's own context, see results/run-1784483812198.json case 20) contains NO opening hours anywhere. These hours are entirely fabricated. This is a direct, confirmed violation of non-negotiable rule #10 (added specifically to prevent this) and the exact failure mode case 20 was designed to catch.

The agent also stated 'Der Beitrag startet ab 29,90 € pro Monat' as if this were the base membership price. The actual profile text says the 29,90 € figure is for a 'Zusatzoption Gerätetraining inkl. Umkleiden, Duschen und Sauna' (an ADD-ON for equipment/shower/sauna access), not a general starting membership fee. The agent took a real number from the profile and reattached it to a different, incorrect claim — a subtler and arguably more dangerous failure mode than pure invention, since the number itself is 'real' and could pass a shallow fact-check.

Correctly treated 'war noch nie im Fitnessstudio' as specifying the functional ask (general fitness) without needing to ask a separate guided-choice question — a defensible reading of implicit intent rather than a rule violation.

Top pick (Praxis Bilal Physiotherapie) is well-grounded to the nervous-beginner driver: profile genuinely states barrier-free access, no long wait times, and 1:1 personal coaching — a substantively better match for this driver than a generic gym, and the agent named the specific concrete details rather than a generic reassurance.
Passes the genericness check in comparison to other cases — tone and content visibly differ from a bare 'Fitness in Münster' request.

Two of the three recommendations (HEINZ training, Vi-Dance) have thin, template-boilerplate profile text ('bietet vielseitige Möglichkeiten im Bereich Ems... Individuelle Trainings- und Nutzungsmöglichkeiten' — generic filler present on many partners with minimal scraped content). The agent's justification for HEINZ ('Einsteiger:innen werden laut Profil von Anfang an individuell beraten und betreut') restates this boilerplate as if it were a specific, meaningful signal about beginner-friendliness — it isn't; it's filler text, not evidence. The agent currently cannot distinguish a genuinely detailed profile from a boilerplate placeholder one.
